result.summary: Do not close the design gate yet: the C1 lossless-deletion claim relies on a stale identity check.

findings.title: A C1 duplicate can become the only copy before pruning
findings.body: C1 proves equivalence during creation, but O2 calls its deletion in a later run unconditionally lossless. The owner can meanwhile delete the announced withheld twin—as the incident runbook instructs—leaving the unrecorded redacted copy as the sole survivor. Executing the actual identity and prune branches against an in-memory filesystem reproduced this: cleanup failed, the twin was removed, and a later prune destroyed the remaining original. O2/O8 and owner item 1 therefore understate the accepted data-loss cases.
findings.recommendation: Describe C1 as a duplicate at creation time only. Condition lossless eviction on an identical twin still existing at deletion time, update the dependent claims, and add regression coverage for twin removal between creation and pruning.

next_steps: Correct the time-dependent classification before dispatching implementation.
